messages:
alejandra: Hey — noticed p99 in the endpoint breakdown for /v1/generate is ~220ms but dashboard aggregate p99 is 780ms. Did a quick compare by region and model; counts match. Anyone see a fanout/fallback causing duplicated slow samples?

mike: Hmm could be fallback routing to warm-up hosts. Did we recently change routing policy to "gradient fallback"? :thinking:

samir: Also check sampling origin — endpoint breakdown aggregates per-shard samples, aggregate uses merged rollups. If merge mode changed to 'weighted' we could be inflating tail.

jia: Can you paste the two screenshots? Also run this debug query against telemetry to compare raw p99s:
```
SELECT
  route,
  percentile(0.99, latency_ms) AS p99,
  sum(count) AS samples
FROM telemetry.latency_rollups
WHERE route = '/v1/generate'
  AND window = '1m'
  AND ts >= now() - interval '15 minutes'
GROUP BY route;
```

alejandra: I'll attach screenshots in thread. Ran the query — endpoint rollups show p99s around 220 then a tiny set of high outliers on node-id 'gpu-11' with latency 1200ms but sample count 3. The aggregate p99 seems pulled to 780. Not sure why aggregate includes those outliers more strongly.

mike: Are those outliers from a canary? Check route tags — rollouts that are tagged with 'staging' used to be excluded from aggregate but if tag merging changed they'd be counted.

samir: Another angle — prefix/KV cache hits are counted separately. If the aggregate includes cache-miss latencies (e.g., first token generation) while endpoint breakdown is post-cache-hit metrics, that explains shift.

alejandra: Good call. Where is the post-cache metric emitted? I thought both metrics used 'serve.latency' but with different tags.

jia: Serve.latency has tag 'cache_status' (hit/miss) but the dashboard percentiles default to show all. Endpoint breakdown UI has an implicit filter 'cache_status=hit' for perceived app latency. We had a recent UX change to collapse filters; maybe someone removed that implicit filter.

console-bot: deploy-1234 finished — changed dashboard aggregation config: collapseFilters=true

mike: That console-bot deploy could be it. We inadvertently started showing all cache statuses in the endpoint breakdown. Fix options:
- Reintroduce implicit filter in UI for endpoint breakdown
- Make aggregate and endpoint dashboards explicit about cache_status
- Adjust rollup service to expose cache-aware percentiles

samir: Short-term: add note on dashboard explaining 'includes cache-misses'. Medium-term: update rollup merge to produce cache-aware percentiles so both views can choose which to surface.

alejandra: I'll open a console PR to re-add implicit filter and a follow-up infra ticket to expose cache-aware rollups. Thanks — tagging @mike @samir @jia for visibility :eyes: 

mike: 👍 also add a quick e2e test in perf-tests that asserts p99(drop cache) >= p99(cache-hit) else fail.

samir: For debugging, here's a quick curl to hit telemetry debug endpoint (only prod-internal):
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://telemetry.internal/api/debug/latencies?route=/v1/generate&since=15m"

jia: assigning myself to the infra ticket. If anyone runs more queries, paste results here.

alejandra: Screenshots and query output attached. Closing loop once PR lands.
